pre_registered: 2026-09-18, frozen before any number in this artifact was computed
what_riv_is_for: RIV+ is a VALUE RECORD, not a forecaster: a leverage-weighted account of the wins a reliever actually added. It is therefore gated DESCRIPTIVELY, against what clubs paid, and the claim it carries is descriptive. Gating it as a forecaster would test a claim it never made.
shipped_eval_defects_addressed: two different targets on two different scales (forward_stability_check)
a pass condition that rewards noise (riv_less_stable_than_rem)
no interval anywhere on the market comparison
a stored 0.02 constant used as a floor
identity by normalized name with no receipts
un-clustered rows although relievers sign in several winters
the eval scored riv_raw while the board serves the re-standardized composite, so pooled across winters they are not the same statistic

v1.target: AAV of the signed contract (raw, pooled across winters)
v1.note: legacy convention; the shipped gate verdicts were established here

v2.target: AAV of the signed contract (within-OUTCOME-season z-score removes the era term)
v2.bootstrap: player-clustered (all of a player's pairs move together), season-stratified (players stratified by first predictor season); 2000 reps, seeded; CIs are wider by design
v2.note: transition-cycle companion; future gates must pre-declare v1 or v2

harness.pair_rule: Y->Y+1 pairs kept only when the OUTCOME season is complete (past Nov 15). Partial-year targets (e.g. mid-2026) are a defect, dropped under BOTH conventions.
harness.predictors: unrounded *_raw model scores (display rounding never enters evals)
interpretation_rules: existing VALIDATED ships STAND even if v2 weakens them; a reversal is flagged to the owner, not auto-reverted
ledgered NO-SHIPs are re-baselined under v2 but never revived by v2 alone
X-R2 / X-S2 flips are not promised

conventions.v1: iid paired resample over matched signings
conventions.v2: player-clustered (all of a player's signings move together), SIGNING-WINTER stratified, because pay levels differ by winter
conventions.mde95: derived in run as 1.645 * bootstrap sd of the gap; the hard-coded 0.02 slack is retired by this gate

B1_primary.estimand: rho(RIV+_served(walk year), AAV) - rho(REM+(walk year), AAV), one target, one scale, same matched rows
B1_primary.target: the AAV of the free-agent contract signed in the winter following the walk year (raw dollars; Spearman, so the shipped log transform is a rank no-op and is labelled as one)
B1_primary.baseline: REM+ (unrounded rem_plus_raw), named explicitly per the owner decision
B1_primary.primary: RIV+_served: the per-season composite re-standardized on its own pool spread, as rem_plus.score_riv_plus ships it

served_integers.note: the comparison a board reader actually makes: the served RIV+ integer against the served REM+ integer

lab_riv_raw_no_restandardize.note: the statistic the SHIPPED eval scored (tools/rem_plus_lab riv_raw, the bare weighted z with no re-standardize). Pooled across winters it is not the same statistic as the served column; this cell is how much that matters here.

B1_primary.rule_note_mis_specification_found_in_run: RECORDED, not edited away. The pre-registered R2-5 middle band ('lo95 <= 0 but lo95 > -MDE95 under both conventions -> stays provisional') is unreachable for a gap centred near zero, and the algebra is one line: lo95 is the 2.5th percentile of the gap draws, roughly mean - 1.96*sd, while -MDE95 is -1.645*sd, so lo95 > -MDE95 requires mean > 0.315*sd. A dead-centre null therefore lands in the REFUTED row rather than the not-separable row. This run is exactly that case (gap mean 0.099 sd). The rule is applied as written because it is harsher than its own stated intent and softening a pre-registered outcome after seeing it is forbidden; the mis-specification is carried here so the NEXT re-gate fixes the band rather than inheriting it. The reading that travels with the verdict is 'not shown to be better', never 'shown to be worse'.

multiplicity.family: one primary test, B1, so k = 1 and Holm is the identity; declared anyway so the family size is on the record

v1.note: uniformly more powerful than Bonferroni and valid under arbitrary dependence. Step 1 uses alpha/k, so a family where nothing clears Bonferroni also clears nothing here.

v2.note: uniformly more powerful than Bonferroni and valid under arbitrary dependence. Step 1 uses alpha/k, so a family where nothing clears Bonferroni also clears nothing here.

disclosure_repeatability_leg.interpretation_fixed_in_advance: If REM+ beats RIV+ at forecasting next-year RIV+, that CONFIRMS RIV+ carries a large non-repeatable deployment and sequencing component, which is consistent with the two-number design and is NOT a failure under the descriptive frame. It does, however, FORBID any forward reading of the RIV+ column, and the glossary and column copy must say so (a display consequence). If RIV+ were to BEAT REM+ at forecasting next-year RIV+, the premise of the two-number design would be wrong and a re-design question would open; it still would not pass this gate, because this gate is the market leg.

RIV+(Y+1).question: does REM+(Y) or RIV+(Y) predict RIV+(Y+1) better

REM+(Y+1).question: does REM+(Y) or RIV+(Y) predict REM+(Y+1) better

coverage.note: Coverage is reported separately and is NEVER used to explain a gap. Identity resolution is the binding constraint on this pair set, so it is reported, never assumed.

retirements: the hard-coded -0.02 slack at tools/rem_plus_lab.py is replaced by an in-run MDE95
riv_less_stable_than_rem is removed as a PASS condition, because a check that a number is noisier than its baseline can be passed by adding noise to it

verdict.reason: REFUTED ON RESOLUTION, and the direction must be said plainly so the row is not misread: the gap POINT ESTIMATE still favours RIV+ (0.5733 vs 0.5665, gap mean 0.0052), but its lower bound sits at or below the in-run MDE95, so the pre-registered rule fires. RIV+ is NOT shown to be worse than REM+; it is shown not to be BETTER, which is the only claim the row made. The published market edge (0.576 vs 0.508) does not survive one target, one scale, the walk-year sample floor and canonical identity: on this pair set REM+ reads 0.5665, not 0.508, and the edge collapses to a coin flip. Whether the column stays on the board is an open question for the display lane.
